title: surge-fence-credit-rebalancer-and-kv-cache-guardrails
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Summary: During a dedicated cluster capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed coordinated eviction storms and persistent tail latency for several tenants. Investigation showed three contributing failures: (1) a burst refill regression that allowed large token bursts beyond reservation budgets, (2) KV cache pollution across tenants causing memory pressure and frequent cache thrashing, and (3) the reservation reconcilier underweighting recent 99th-percentile usage which mis-sized reservations after a traffic shift.

Impact: Multiple mid-market Dedicated customers experienced sustained request 503s for 12-18 minutes and elevated p99 latencies (from ~220ms to >3s) for ~40 minutes. Cost: emergency scale-up and customer escalations.

Root cause analysis (brief):
- Burst tokenbucket change (PR #github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2045) introduced an overly generous refill window to reduce sustained error loops; this allowed rapid burst replenishment that bypassed reservation checks under certain scheduler paths.
- KV cache lacked enforced tenant caps; long-running beam workloads from a single tenant filled shared GPU RAM and caused eviction cascades for co-located tenants.
- Reservation reconciliation algorithm used an EWMA with a long half-life (24h) which failed to capture a sudden shift in traffic, so reservations were undersized when the surge hit.

Scope of this ticket: implement a three-pronged follow-up covering immediate mitigations, medium-term correctness fixes, and monitoring/guardrail enhancements to prevent recurrence. This ticket coordinates owners, rollout, and verification criteria.
action_items: Hotfix: clamp burst-refill window to pre-regression default and add a safety-check that refuses refill when reservation_headroom < 10% (owner: Arjun) — deploy canary within 48h and monitor p99 and eviction rate.

KV cache protection: implement per-tenant soft cap with token-based eviction priority and a hard OOM breaker that rejects requests when a tenant exceeds 75% of GPU KV pool (owner: Linh) — roll out in two phases: feature flag then default-on.

Reservation reconcilier: update metric to incorporate 99th-percentile over rolling 2-hour window plus a short-term burst buffer; add automated backfill recalculation after detected traffic shift (owner: Priya) — include unit tests and simulation harness.

Observability: add new dashboard panels (eviction rate by tenant, KV cache residency by tenant, refill events per minute) and set alert thresholds (p95 eviction rate > 0.5%/min) (owner: Michael) — link dashboards in comments.

Chaos + Synthetic: add a synthetic workload scenario that simulates a heavy-beam tenant and a concurrent small-tenant mix to CI load generator so we can validate isolation guarantees (owner: Sato) — target: add to nightly suite.

Runbook update: add emergency mitigation steps (soft-fence tenant, clamp refill, increase eviction grace) and postmortem checklist for SRE rotations (owner: Maya) — update Confluence and embed links in console incident flow.
Customer communications: prepare one-pager for affected customers summarizing cause, technical fixes, and SLA remediation plan (owner: Customer Success) — coordinate with Legal for language.
Post-deploy validation: define metrics gating for scaling down emergency capacity and record a 72h stability window before closing the ticket (owner: Arjun & Priya).

verification_criteria: Canary measurements show p99 latency <= 350ms and eviction rate at baseline for 48h after hotfix rollout.
KV per-tenant cap prevents a single tenant from exceeding 60% of KV pool in synthetic stress test (runbook attached).
Reservation reconcilier reduces frequency of manual reservation adjustments by >80% on simulated traffic shift scenarios.
Alerting and dashboard coverage in place and reviewed by SRE and Observability leads.
